audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows contradicted their whys. win[0] and win[1] read Dr. Mundo and Skill while whys[0] and whys[1] both say 'Yone-favoured'; win[3] and win[4] read Yone and Dr. Mundo while whys[3] and whys[4] both say 'Skill'. The drmundo__yone mirror describes the same three fabricated Dr. Mundo windows and flipped four rows as one group; the packet chart is Yone/Yone/Yone/Skill/Skill/Yone/Yone.
audit.why: Chart, whys, packet and mirror all agree — only the rendered rows were wrong.
audit.corrected: win[0]/win[1] = Yone, win[3]/win[4] = Skill, with the matching phases[].side. Ratings on the two flipped Dr. Mundo rows raised from 3/10 to 6/10 to match the other Yone/Skill rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns, and Maximum Dosage is described only as 'a big heal and MS'.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s, Infected Bonesaw is 4s from 975 range, and Maximum Dosage is a flat 120s that instantly restores a percentage of MISSING health — meaning the lower you burst him, the more it gives back. Grievous Wounds has to be on him before he casts it, not after.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into spikes[0], spikes[1], mid, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Goes Where He Pleases is never mentioned anywhere on the page. It resists the FIRST immobilising effect that hits him — which is your Mortal Steel knock-up, and the pull on Fate Sealed. Separately, phases[4].why and breakdown.late both describe Fate Sealed as setting up 'team knockups nothing can dodge'; it blinks behind the last champion in a line and PULLS everyone toward you.
audit.why: A Yone who opens with the Q3 knock-up gets it eaten by the passive and then commits into a target he never actually locked down. And spacing for a knock-up when the ability pulls sends your team the wrong way.
audit.corrected: Passive written into breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[0].d and spikes[0]; Fate Sealed corrected to blink-and-pull in phases[4].why and breakdown.late, matching the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] calls his Q 'Infected Cleaver'. The ability is Infected Bonesaw.
audit.why: Infected Cleaver is a different champion's ability name entirely.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Dr. Mundo's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind the last target and pulls. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Maximum Dosage heals him right back.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge — build your teamfight around that. Dr. Mundo carry threat: 8/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls everyone toward you — build the fight around that. Dr. Mundo carry threat: 8/10 — anti-heal stays core if he gets ahead.

edits.before: You dominate early: Mundo's only poke is his Infected Bonesaw (Q) cleaver, which you sidestep with E, and his passive regen can't keep up with your Q-stack autos plus W shield trades.
edits.after: You dominate early, but his passive eats your first immobilise — the Q3 knock-up gets spent, so plan a second. Infected Bonesaw (4s, 975 range) is his only poke, and your Q-stack autos out-trade his regen.

edits.before: Mundo R Maximum Dosage gives him a big heal and MS, but he has no lockdown to catch you, so you disengage with E-return and re-engage on your terms.
edits.after: Maximum Dosage (R, 120s) instantly heals a share of his MISSING health — land Grievous Wounds before he casts it. He has no lockdown, so you still leave on your terms.

edits.before: The Skill window at 4-5 is just his cleaver poke stacking up if you get careless; play around dodging Q and your Mortal Steel keeps out-trading his regen, though you won't outright kill a tank.
edits.after: The Skill window at 4-5 is his Bonesaw poke stacking up — it is a 4s cooldown, so dodging one is not enough. Mortal Steel still out-trades his regen, but you will not outright kill a tank.

edits.before: Dodge his Cleaver (Q) with E so he can't chunk you or slow you
edits.after: Dodge Infected Bonesaw (Q) so he cannot chunk you or slow you

edits.before: Land Infected Cleaver (Q) to poke and slow you
edits.after: Land Infected Bonesaw (Q) to poke and slow you

edits.before: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — His sustain + reset. Poke around it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Goes Where He Pleases: his passive eats your first immobilise, so the Q3 knock-up is spent breaking it, not landing it. - Heart Zapper: 17s at rank 1, healing off stored damage. - Infected Bonesaw: 4s, 975 range.

edits.before: His sustain + reset. Poke around it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 17s at rank 1 — it stores the damage you deal and heals him off the burst.

edits.before: That is Dr. Mundo's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: His passive eats your first knock-up, so it is the second one that lands.

notes: The biggest gap was Goes Where He Pleases, which appeared nowhere despite being the reason Yone's opening knock-up does nothing to him. Also carried the champion-wide Fate Sealed error the mirror flagged: it is a blink-behind plus a pull toward you, not a knock-up, and that wording was in both phases[4].why and breakdown.late. Ratings on the two flipped Dr. Mundo rows were raised to 6/10 to match the other Yone/Skill rows; if the intended rating scale differs, those two edits can be dropped without affecting the sides.
